gaps.sentence: The prototype is undeniably elegant; it is, ___, hopelessly impractical.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' concedes elegance while introducing the drawback.

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: Take a map ___ you get lost in the backstreets.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something that might happen.

gaps.sentence: ___ she now lives in Oslo, she still supports the Dublin club.
gaps.explanation: 'Although' introduces the contrasting clause; 'despite' needs a noun phrase.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is priceless; ___, it is far too fragile to display.
gaps.explanation: 'However' marks the contrast between value and fragility.

gaps.sentence: The flat is spacious and well located; ___, the rent is surprisingly low.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds another supporting point in the same direction.

gaps.sentence: The treatment doesn't weaken patients; ___, it speeds up their recovery.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' asserts the opposite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.
